prompt:
Write a React 19 counter context in TypeScript (strict mode) that is split so that components which only change the count never re-render when it changes.

Export:
- `function CounterProvider({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode })` (you may import the `ReactNode` type from `react`).
- `function useCount(): number` -- the current count of the nearest `CounterProvider`.
- `function useCountActions(): { increment(): void; decrement(): void; reset(): void }` -- `increment` adds 1, `decrement` subtracts 1 (the count may go negative), `reset` sets it back to 0.

Behaviour:
- The count of each `CounterProvider` starts at 0; separate providers keep separate counts.
- A component that calls `useCountActions()` but not `useCount()` must NOT re-render when the count changes (it is rendered as a child of the provider and nothing else re-renders it).
- `useCountActions()` returns the very same object (same identity) on every render for the whole lifetime of the provider.
- Calling `useCount()` or `useCountActions()` in a component that has no `CounterProvider` above it throws an `Error`.

Use only `react`. Answer with a single ```tsx code block containing only the module.
